To summarize, the key findings of our research, stated in one sentence that includes all relevant information, are that
the anthrax toxin is endocytosed in a lipid raft–dependent manner.
the anthrax toxin triggers the internalization of its receptor via lipid rafts–mediated clatrin-dependent endocytosis.
the anthrax toxin triggers endocytic uptake of its cell surface receptor by a lipid raft–dependent mechanism.
In summary, our research is concerned with
understanding the mechanism of internalization of anthrax toxin and how this process can be exploited to develop novel therapeutic agents.
the mechanisms of internalization of the anthrax lethal factor and its receptor.
the molecular basis of the interaction of the anthrax lethal toxin with its receptor and with the mechanism of its uptake.
In summary, a comprehensive and detailed conclusive statement would be that
the anthrax toxin exploits the endocytic pathway for internalization, which is a novel and important aspect of its mode of action.
the anthrax toxin is an ideal model to study the role of lipid rafts in endocytosis.
the ATR is an endocytic receptor that can internalize in a slow, constitutive manner or in a rapid and highly efficient manner when clustered.
A comprehensive summary for our work would be that
anthrax toxin uses the ATR as a Trojan horse for its entry into cells.
clustering of the ATR into lipid rafts is necessary and sufficient for efficient endocytosis and delivery of the lethal toxin to the cytoplams.

the slow endocytosing ATR can be rapidly endocytosed when it is clustered into rafts by the heptameric anthrax toxin or by an antibody sandwich, and that this process can be blocked by drugs that interfere with lipid raft integrity.
The main takeaway from our work is that

the ATR is not a classical endocytic receptor, but its endocytosis is facilitated by its ability to form heptameric complexes that can be clustered by PA or by antibody cross-linking, which allows its recruitment into lipid rafts and subsequent uptake by a clathrin-dependent mechanism.
clustering of the receptor into lipid rafts is necessary for efficient internalization and delivery of LF into the cytosol.
clustering of the ATR into lipid rafts is necessary to trigger endocytosis and delivery of LF to cytoplasm.
